Fit the logistic model with fixed provider effects

Source: R/model_logistic_fe.R
fit_logistic_fe.Rd

Fits \(\mathrm{logit}\, p_{ij} = \gamma_i + Z_{ij}^\top\beta\) with a binary or binomial outcome (\(Y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bin}(N_{ij}, p_{ij})\)) by the serial blockwise inversion Newton (SerBIN) or block ascent Newton (BAN) algorithm, on the providers that pp_data() marked as included, optionally with Firth's penalty.

Usage

fit_logistic_fe(
  data,
  algorithm = c("SerBIN", "BAN"),
  penalty = c("none", "firth"),
  max_iter = 10000,
  tol = 1e-05,
  bound = 10,
  backtrack = TRUE,
  threads = 1,
  stop = c("beta", "relch", "ratch", "all", "or"),
  auc = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data() with a binary or binomial outcome.

algorithm

"SerBIN" (default; Wu et al. 2022) or "BAN" (He et al. 2013).

penalty

"none" (default; maximum likelihood) or "firth" (penalized likelihood with Jeffreys' prior, Firth 1993), which keeps the effects of providers with no or all events finite.

max_iter

maximum number of iterations. Default 10,000.

tol

convergence tolerance. Default 1e-5.

bound

provider effects are kept within median(gamma) +/- bound during the iterations. Default 10.

backtrack

use a backtracking line search (not used with the Firth penalty). Default TRUE.

threads

number of OpenMP threads for the information matrix (SerBIN and Firth). Results do not depend on it.

stop

stopping rule: "beta" (default; infinity norm of the change in beta), "relch" (relative change in the log-likelihood), "ratch" (change relative to the total change since the start), "all" (all three below tol) or "or" (any of the three below tol). With the Firth penalty the rules read the penalized log-likelihood.

auc

also compute the area under the ROC curve (binary outcomes).

message

print the iteration history.

Value

An object of class logistic_fe:

coefficients

a list with gamma (provider effects, named by provider) and beta (covariate coefficients, named by covariate).

fitted

fitted probabilities of the included rows.

linear_predictor

\(Z\hat\beta\) of the included rows.

loglik, aic, bic

binomial log-likelihood (without the constant \(\log\binom{N}{Y}\)) and the information criteria.

penalized_loglik

the penalized log-likelihood (Firth only).

auc

the AUC, when requested (NA for binomial outcomes).

data

the included rows, as sorted by pp_data().

vars, sizes, cutoff

from pp_data() (sizes restricted to the included providers).

rows

rows per provider, in the order of coefficients$gamma.

control

the settings and the number of iterations.

converged

whether the stopping rule was met before max_iter.

Details

SerBIN updates provider effects and covariate coefficients jointly using the block structure of the information matrix; BAN alternates between the two blocks. Providers with no or all events are fitted (their effects sit at the bound); the tests treat them as the data allow.

With penalty = "firth" the penalized log-likelihood \(\ell(\gamma, \beta) + \frac12 \log\det I(\gamma, \beta)\) is maximized by a joint Newton step through the same block structure; the modified score adds \(h_{ij}(\frac12 - p_{ij})\) to each row's residual, with \(h_{ij}\) the row's leverage \(N_{ij} p_{ij}(1 - p_{ij})\, x_{ij}^\top I^{-1} x_{ij}\). The estimates stay finite when a provider has no or all events. The computation follows ParaFLR (Shao and He, the paraflr package in UM-KevinHe/hpc-flr): the provider is the unit of parallel work, so the per-provider information blocks, leverages and scores are spread over threads; the results do not depend on the number of threads. loglik, aic and bic report the unpenalized log-likelihood at the penalized estimate; the penalized value is penalized_loglik.

References

Firth D (1993). Bias reduction of maximum likelihood estimates. Biometrika, 80(1), 27-38.

Shao Y, He K. ParaFLR: parallel Firth-corrected logistic regression with high-dimensional provider effects. https://github.com/UM-KevinHe/hpc-flr

He K, Kalbfleisch JD, Li Y, Li Y (2013). Evaluating hospital readmission rates in dialysis facilities; adjusting for hospital effects. Lifetime Data Analysis, 19, 490-512.

Wu W, Yang Y, Kang J, He K (2022). Improving large-scale estimation and inference for profiling health care providers. Statistics in Medicine, 41(15), 2840-2853.

See also

test(), summary(), standardize(), confint.logistic_fe()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_fe(pd)
fit
#> Logistic model with fixed provider effects (SerBIN)
#>   2679 rows, 20 providers, 3 covariates; binary outcome
#>   log-likelihood -1336.52; iterations 5
#>   provider effects: median -1.08, range -1.823058 to  0.006187
coef(fit)$beta
#>         x1         x2         x3 
#>  0.5942121 -0.4515167  0.3261670 
fit_firth <- fit_logistic_fe(pd, penalty = "firth")
